text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--Denmark's main right-wing opposition parties led by the Liberals and Conservatives would win a combined absolute majority of 91 seats in the 179-seat parliament if elections were held now, a new opinion poll shows. Elections are due again in Denmark in September 1998 at the latest. A Social Democrat-led centre-left coalition is in power at present.

--Denmark's Maastricht Treaty opt-outs on joint European defence, a single currency and legal and police cooperation are a bagatelle compared with the expansion of EU to embrace eastern Europe countries, economy minister Marianne Jelved said. She said it would be tragic if Denmark's opt-outs barred EU from expanding eastwards.

--Danish environment minister Svend Auken is to fight against any European Union approval of the weedkiller Paraquat, which the East Asiatic Company(EAC) produces in a joint venture with a British company in Thailand. Danish European parliament members are campaigning to ban the use and export of the weedkiller and Auken has asked EAC to give a full account of safety measures. Investors are threatening to withdraw share capital from EAC in protest against its Paraquat production.
